method: the host bundle is installed into a run-owned test home and the shared runtime modules are linked into it, so the fence resolves the seam from the same base a real worker uses

outcomeMeaning.LIMIT_NO_LABEL_WRITE: the seam resolved but no label could be written on this volume; behavioural compatibility is NOT established
outcomeMeaning.LABEL_NOT_APPLIED: the write claimed success and left no label; this is the silent no-op the plan warns about
outcomeMeaning.LIMIT_NO_LOW_INTEGRITY_MECHANISM: a label was written but no Low-integrity process was available to test the refusal, so the enforcement question is UNTESTED rather than failed
outcomeMeaning.LIMIT_LOW_DRIVER_FAILED: the Low-integrity driver failed before the probe executed, so nothing was read and neither a refusal nor a disclosure is claimed
outcomeMeaning.LIMIT_LOW_CONTROL_UNREADABLE: the Low process could not read the unlabelled control either, so a refusal cannot be attributed to the label
outcomeMeaning.PROTECTED: the label was written through rc.3, read back, and a LOW-integrity read was refused while the unlabelled control succeeded
outcomeMeaning.NOT_REFUSED: a Low-integrity process read the labelled content; a disclosure, never a pass

arms.question: is the module graph established so the seam can resolve from the test home?
does the fence resolve the seam from the test home, and what version does it report?
is the bound Win32 label API usable?
was an explicit DACL grant applied to the labelled fixtures?
can a mandatory label be written through the installed rc.3 seam?

writeOutcome.detail: verified by readback: integrity=Medium policies=[NO_READ_UP] flags=3 mask=0x2

arms.question: does the label read back after the write?
is the UNLABELLED control readable, so a refused read elsewhere is meaningful?
is a LOW-integrity process refused when it reads the labelled directory?
arms.observation: REFUSED at Low integrity (EPERM) while the unlabelled control read succeeded — this is the Mandatory Integrity mechanism

arms.question: does the SAME-integrity read succeed? (it must, and that is not a disclosure)
arms.observation: the Medium-integrity read SUCCEEDS, which is expected: NO_READ_UP forbids reads by LOWER integrity, not equal

arms.question: is a labelled LINK treated as coverage of its unlabelled target?
arms.observation: the external target is still readable, so the link is not coverage

arms.question: does koffi resolve from the seam package's declared graph at the qualified version?
is the fixture still the object this run created?
arms.observation: every fixture is inside the run-owned test home
